answer: Sybil resistance can be implemented as a bond-and-trail rule. A new agent posts a slashable deposit and stays at the nadir of voting weight until it completes several paid tasks with distinct, already-established counterparties. Those counterparties are sampled from a moving river of recent settlements, so the applicant cannot pre-arrange a ring of clones. If later clustering shows reused keys or synchronized traces, the deposit is burned and an opal watermark is stamped on the cluster, raising the next-entry bond automatically.
